text: HR reports that the New Hire Onboarding flow is stuck. Maria Chen started yesterday, and none of her onboarding tasks fired automatically. The flow has run successfully for every other new hire, so HR assumes it's now broken and asks you to fix it.

Resist the instinct to start rereading the flow's logic. Go straight to the execution log and find the specific run triggered by Maria's record creation. It isn't marked failed — it's marked waiting, sitting at an Approval action called Manager Approval, New Hire Equipment Request.

Expand that step and look at what the approver pill actually resolved to. It's empty. The flow correctly tried to route the approval to the new hire's manager, read from her User record — there just isn't one on file for her, so nobody was ever notified, and the approval has been silently waiting on a response that can never arrive.

This is the key moment: separate two problems that look identical from outside. The flow performed exactly as designed, reading the manager field and routing the approval exactly the way it was built to. The real defect is upstream — a data quality gap. Maria's manager field was never populated when her account was created, most likely because whoever provisioned it didn't have her manager finalized yet.

The real fix has two parts. Immediately, populate her manager field and resubmit the approval so onboarding continues today. Durably, add a check before the Approval action: if the manager field is blank, route instead to a default fallback approver, like an HR lead, instead of silently stalling.

A stuck flow is very often accurately reflecting bad or missing data, not malfunctioning. Reading the execution log first is what turns an afternoon of rereading flow actions into a five-minute diagnosis. Next, Chapter 8 begins: your own capstone flow, start to finish.
